A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LoRA-Ensemble. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original classification, calibration, OOD detection, efficiency, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, corruption tests, and controlled analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Figure 1 retain the frozen shared backbone, member-specific low-rank attention updates, classification heads, and prediction aggregation. The new configurations in Appendix G are ablation arms; the CNN adaptation already appeared in v4.

E1.justification: Appendix A.8 adds systematic classification under corrupted inputs using CIFAR-10-C and CIFAR-100-C, covering 19 corruption types at five severities. This substantially extends input-condition coverage beyond the existing clean-image and semantic OOD evaluations. Audio and SST-2 coverage already existed in v4.

E2.justification: v5 adds Last-layer Ensemble, SNGP, and EpiNet to CIFAR-100 comparisons; L2 and LRFormer to HAM10000; EpiNet to OOD detection; and Bayes-LoRA to SST-2. These are reported comparisons in Tables 1, 2, 4, and 8, extending several comparator families.

E3.justification: v5 adds FPR@95%TPR, peak GPU-memory measurements, corruption-severity evaluation, and protocols for new controlled experiments. Appendix I specifies rank-2 adaptation for one epoch without warmup after training the backbone on HAM10000. Newly disclosed HAM10000 splitting and ECE binning do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test corruption robustness, the relationship between initialization gain and weight diversity, attention versus MLP adapter placement, trainable embeddings, shared versus separate classification heads, and adaptation of a backbone trained on the target dataset. These extend v4's existing rank, initialization, backbone-size, and temperature-scaling studies.

E5.justification: Appendices R.5–R.6 add explicit per-member seed specifications for Last-layer Ensemble and EpiNet. The general five-run, one-standard-deviation reporting practice remains; three iNaturalist runs were already stated in v4's results table. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: v5 adds substantial baseline, corruption, and ablation results while retaining the main classification scores. OOD values change: LoRA-Ensemble's CIFAR-10 AUPRC changes from 84.1 to 80.4 and SVHN AUPRC from 80.9 to 95.2. Reported ViT training and inference times also change, from 1108 seconds and 22.7 milliseconds to 1832 seconds and 14.8 milliseconds.

T1.justification: Appendix E introduces a diversity-score definition based on inter-member weight correlations. Appendix R.9 adds formal SNGP formulations and discussion of its Lipschitz assumptions. The central LoRA equations and existing Batch-Ensemble gradient derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the main novelty and performance claims. The introduction narrows architectural compatibility from broadly architecture-independent transformers to standard self-attention architectures and explicitly includes language evaluation in the contribution list.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations of Bayesian-LoRA tradeoffs, excessive diversity, component placement, and adaptation on the backbone's training dataset. It reframes training time as comparable to Explicit Ensemble and adds practical calibration guidance. The finite-ensemble posterior-extension discussion is replaced by limitations concerning MoE and nonstandard attention architectures.

D1.justification: v5 adds baseline implementation listings, architecture and optimization specifications, Bayesian posterior-sampling settings, and the SNGP hyperparameter table. It newly discloses HAM10000's stratified 80/20 image-level split without patient or lesion grouping and specifies ten equally spaced ECE bins. These materially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Related work and positioning expand substantially around Bayesian LoRA, Laplace approximations, EpiNet, SNGP, Lipschitz-constrained attention, and corruption robustness. Sections 5–6 and Appendix R develop explicit comparisons and compatibility arguments. The concurrent LoRA-ensemble work already cited in v4 remains acknowledged.

P1.justification: Section 3 is reorganized into explicit setup, baseline, compute, and task subsections. Previously dispersed baseline appendices are consolidated under Appendix R, and the discussion gains dedicated comparison and guidance passages. Citation style and wording also change throughout.

P2.justification: v5 changes typography, margins, headers, author layout, and float placement throughout. The computational-cost table moves from the main text to Appendix A.9 and gains memory columns. New corruption figures, ablation tables, and implementation listings accompany expanded baseline and OOD tables; existing analytical figures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: New corruption tests and component controls address gaps in v4's empirical support, while expanded baseline documentation and evaluation disclosures improve transparency. Reporting problems limit the net gain: v5's universal OOD-superiority statement conflicts with Table 4's CIFAR-10 AUPRC values, 80.4 versus Split-Ensemble's 81.7. Appendix R.8 also supports its Bayesian-LoRA speed claim using a stale ViT/CIFAR-100 timing for comparison with BERT/SST-2.
